analysis.title: US manufacturing benefiting from a strong economy, tech investment, tariffs and energy security
key_insights: October ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 from 54.5 in September. The market had expected it to stay at 54.5.
ISM production index rose to 59.0 from 56.7, a five-year high. New orders are at 55.5 and the order backlog at 54.6, both above the 50 break-even level.
ISM employment slipped to 52.4 from 52.7. ING says manufacturing should still add to Friday's payrolls figure. Prices paid are 75.2, in line with the six-month average.

ING says tariffs, US energy security and stronger US growth than other major markets have made US manufacturing more attractive. High value-added manufacturing (tech, electronics, transport, power-related) has significantly outperformed other sectors, and ING expects that to continue.

ING says traditional, labour-intensive, commoditised manufacturing will keep shrinking under foreign competition. Tariffs do not offset the high cost of US production, and retaliatory tariffs hurt these producers abroad.

Construction spending fell 1.9% MoM in September after a 2% rise in August (first reported as +0.9%). Residential construction rose 3.6% MoM in August, then fell 5.5% in September, and the trend is downward on poor affordability at higher mortgage rates.

Non-residential construction growth is concentrated in data centres, up 8.6% MoM and 90.3% YoY. Other non-residential construction outside data centres and electric power is flat. ING reads this as interest-rate-sensitive sectors struggling while tech and AI spending stays strong.
ING says more countries raising military spending may strengthen order books at US defence companies.

Rising military spending in more countries may strengthen order books for US defence companies.
Spending is trending down on lack of affordability with higher mortgage rates.
Spending is up 90.3% YoY and the pipeline stays strong on tech and AI demand.
